note.text: Producer cooperatives can support members’ production or marketing; consumer cooperatives serve purchasing needs; credit cooperatives concern members’ financial services subject to applicable rules. Benefits may include pooled purchasing, shared facilities and bargaining, while finance, management or participation problems remain possible. A surplus may support reserves, development or members under valid rules. One member, one vote does not mean every payment must be shared equally. A patronage allocation can reflect eligible transactions, as the exercise explicitly states.

sections.heading: Your goal and connections
sections.text: By the end, you should be able to identify the service supplied by different cooperatives and calculate an allocation under an explicit rule. Builds on: member ownership and democratic control. Leads to: public ownership and comparison of enterprise objectives.

sections.heading: Understand the economics
sections.text: Producer cooperatives can support members’ production or marketing; consumer cooperatives serve purchasing needs; credit cooperatives concern members’ financial services subject to applicable rules. Benefits may include pooled purchasing, shared facilities and bargaining, while finance, management or participation problems remain possible. A surplus may support reserves, development or members under valid rules. One member, one vote does not mean every payment must be shared equally. A patronage allocation can reflect eligible transactions, as the exercise explicitly states.

sections.heading: Follow the local case
sections.text: A fictional consumer cooperative buys goods for members; a growers’ cooperative arranges shared marketing. After meeting costs, each must follow its rules about reserves and distributions. The classroom allocation uses only the explicitly distributable amount, not all receipts, and does not promise that any real cooperative will pay a return.

sections.heading: Reason and check
sections.text: Name the service before naming the type. Separate voting equality from transaction-based allocation. Deduct or reserve amounts only when specified; do not distribute a reserve already excluded from the distributable total. Explain a benefit alongside the condition needed to achieve it.

questions.prompt: A fictional cooperative allocates {total} CFA francs for patronage-based distribution. The stated member’s eligible purchases are {member} out of all eligible purchases of {allp} CFA francs. Using purchases alone as the agreed basis, calculate the member’s allocation.

misconceptions.explain: That is the entire distribution, not one member’s fraction.
That is transaction value, not the resulting surplus allocation.

solution: Use the member’s eligible transactions as a fraction of all eligible transactions.
